steps.title: P1 obtains promises
steps.narration: A, B, and C persist promises for ballot 7 and report no prior accepted value.
steps.outcome: P1 may enter the accept phase with blue.
steps.invariant: An acceptor rejects ballots lower than its durable promised ballot.

steps.title: Blue is chosen by a majority
steps.narration: A, B, and C accept blue at ballot 7, forming a three-of-five quorum.
steps.outcome: Blue has been chosen even if P1 fails before announcing it.
steps.invariant: A value is chosen only after one quorum accepts the same ballot-value pair.

steps.title: P2 preempts with ballot 8
steps.narration: P2 prepares C, D, and E; all promise ballot 8, and intersecting acceptor C reports blue@7.
steps.outcome: The new quorum discovers the previously accepted chosen value.
steps.invariant: Any two majorities intersect in at least one acceptor.

steps.title: Later proposer adopts blue
steps.narration: The phase-one rule replaces P2’s red preference with the value from the highest accepted ballot it observed.
action: return highest accepted blue@7; adopt blue
steps.outcome: Ballot 8 is constrained to propose blue rather than red.
steps.invariant: A proposer with promises must use the value from the highest accepted ballot returned, if any.

steps.title: Second quorum confirms the same value
steps.narration: C, D, and E accept blue at ballot 8, creating a different quorum without changing the decision.
steps.outcome: Both successful quorums choose blue across leadership change.
steps.invariant: No two quorums can choose different values for the same consensus instance.

production.scenario: An identity platform enables emergency challenge mode only after a quorum-backed policy store accepts the change, so every regional gateway converges on one login policy during an attack.
components: Lets the fraud team switch login challenge mode during an active credential-stuffing attack

Drives the emergency-policy rollback once attack traffic returns to baseline
flows: enable challenge-all mode for consumer login
The abuse desk initiates an emergency sign-in policy change while attack traffic is still rising.
write policy version 611 with quorum durability
The risk API waits for quorum-backed acceptance instead of treating one local write as authoritative.
Once the quorum accepts the change, the decision ledger stores the reason code and exact policy payload.
Every regional gateway reads the same chosen policy version before challenging new login attempts.
Operators can watch whether emergency MFA is suppressing the live attack from the same gateway fleet that enforces it.
When the attack subsides, rollback uses the same quorum path so the system cannot split into mixed login policies.
